chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Ja‘far al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā‘īl, from Abī al-Magh rā’, from Abī Basīr, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him say: The Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him) said, 'Women are the coolness of my eyes, and my two flowers are al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon them).'

key_terms.رَيْحَانَتَايَ: My two flowers (metaphor for beloved, fragrant, and cherished ones)
key_terms.قُرَّةُ الْعَيْنِ: Coolness of the eye (metaphor for joy, comfort, and delight)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the status of women and his grandsons Hasan and Husayn?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the general category of women as the 'coolness of his eyes' and the specific, elevated status of al-Hasan and al-Husayn as his 'two flowers' (rayḥānatay), a term denoting fragrant delight and spiritual purity. This distinction underscores the unique metaphysical rank of the Imams within Shia theology, linking their affection to the concept of *mawaddah* mentioned in the Quran. The hadith serves as a foundational proof for the obligation of loving the Ahl al-Bayt, framing it not merely as emotional attachment but as a divine command tied to the Prophet's own spiritual joy.
